name: Kelso
tax_rate: 2% state-shared basic plus a special hotel/motel tax of 2% (under 40 rooms) or 3% (40 or more rooms) per DOR rate flyer; DOR 2024 shows $219,868 state-shared, $0 special
deadline_pattern: Applications open in early August and close in late August for the following calendar year (Aug 23, 2024 for 2025; Aug 24, 2026 for 2027); LTAC reviews in mid-to-late September and council approves in early October
typical_open: Early August (press release August 4, 2026 for the 2027 cycle)
annual_pool: 2026 cycle: $210,000 from the year's fund plus $84,000 from reserves, $294,000 total available; 2024 lodging tax distributions $219,868 (DOR)
contact: Jessica Bronstein, Executive/Legal Assistant, City Manager's Office, jbronstein@kelso.gov, 360-577-3379; 203 S. Pacific Ave, P.O. Box 819, Kelso, WA 98626
notes: Kelso runs a straightforward annual Lodging Tax Fund request through the City Manager's Office: packets go out in early August, proposals (original plus 5 copies) are due in late August, the Lodging Tax Advisory Committee reviews them at an open afternoon meeting in September, and council adopts the recommendations at its next meeting in early October. The 2026 round awarded $100,000 each to Tam O'Shanter Park and the Kelso Longview Chamber Visitor Information Center, $25,000 to the Kelso Highlander Festival, $11,500 to the Braided 64 wrestling tournament, $10,000 to S'quatchfest and $2,500 to Lights in the Park. Only public agencies and nonprofits may apply; priority goes to overnight stays in Kelso lodging, visitors from outside Cowlitz County, documented economic benefit and a track record. Funding is reimbursement-only under a Municipal Services Contract with insurance naming the city.

presentation.pattern: No presentation step is described; LTAC reviews written proposals at an open meeting in mid-to-late September (Sept 17, 2025 at 3:30 p.m.; Sept 28, 2022 at 3:00 p.m.) that applicants may attend
presentation.format: Open committee meeting at Kelso City Hall council chambers; attendance optional

meeting_schedule: LTAC meets once a year in September to review applications (Sept 17, 2025; Sept 28, 2022); council acts at its next regular meeting in early October (Oct 7, 2025)
pool_note: 2026 cycle: $210,000 current-year fund plus $84,000 reserves = $294,000 available. $100,000 went to Tam O'Shanter Park, a city-owned park, leaving about $194,000 for outside applicants; the Chamber VIC takes $100,000 of that through the same application. KLOG reported total awards of $235,000 while the listed awards sum to $249,000; the discrepancy is unexplained.

name: Sunnyside
tax_rate: 4% (2% state-shared plus 2% special hotel/motel tax per DOR rate flyer; DOR 2024 distributions $73,505 in each column); imposed under Ordinance No. 1973
deadline_pattern: RFP published mid-October with proposals due mid-November at 5 p.m. for the following calendar year (Nov 12, 2026 for 2027); LTAC reviews four days later and council adopts in late November. Earlier cycles ran a first round in late August with a second round in late November if money remained.
typical_open: Mid-October (RFP published October 14, 2026; earlier cycles opened in late July)
annual_pool: 2026: beginning fund balance about $205,000 plus an estimated $120,000 in 2026 lodging tax, about $325,000 combined, with LTAC keeping part in reserve; 2026 recommendations totaled $116,500; 2024 DOR distributions $147,011
contact: Katie Emery, City Clerk, kemery@sunnyside-wa.gov; Miranda Maravilla, Deputy City Clerk, mmaravilla@sunnyside-wa.gov, 509-836-6305; Jessica Mejia, Finance Supervisor, 509-836-6005, jmejia@sunnyside-wa.gov; submit to cityclerk@sunnyside-wa.gov or 818 E. Edison Ave, Sunnyside, WA 98944
notes: Sunnyside's 2027 Lodging Tax Funding RFP is open now: proposals (one document per project, plus W-9, $2M liability insurance and a city-endorsed business license) are due November 12, 2026 at 5 p.m. to the City Clerk, LTAC meets November 16, 2026 from 4 to 7 p.m. where each submitter gets a three-minute pitch, council acts November 25, 2026, award letters go out in December and the funding period is calendar 2027 with reimbursement requests due within 30 days of completion. The committee is Deputy Mayor Julia Hart (council), Tom Denlea (lodging collector), Sierra Foster and Monica Niemeyer (users), with one collector seat vacant. For 2026 LTAC recommended $116,500 (Cinco de Mayo $30,000, Sunshine Days $20,000, Summer Ale Fest $15,000, Veterans Plaza $10,000, Lighted Farm Implement Parade $5,000, American Hill Climb $5,000, Show & Shine $1,500) out of roughly $325,000 on hand, declining Miss Sunnyside and the Nitro Nationals; it wants advertising beyond a 50-mile radius, October-April overnight stays and 'heads in beds' growth before raising awards. For-profit applicants are admitted by the RFP.

presentation.pattern: LTAC review meeting about four days after the deadline (Nov 16, 2026, 4-7 p.m.); each submitter may pitch for three minutes
presentation.format: Three-minute in-person pitch to LTAC at Sunnyside City Hall; attendance encouraged but the RFP calls it optional

meeting_schedule: As needed; the annual review meeting is held in mid-November (Nov 16, 2026, 4-7 p.m.; Nov 13, 2025; Nov 27, 2024)
pool_note: LTAC's November 2025 discussion put about $325,000 on the table ($205,000 fund balance plus roughly $120,000 projected 2026 revenue) but recommended only $116,500 and chose to hold the rest in reserve; the awards listed in the press sum to $86,500 against a $116,500 headline, an unexplained $30,000 gap. No standing commitments to the city itself were identified.

tax_rate: 2% state-shared basic plus a 2% special hotel/motel tax per DOR rate flyer; DOR 2024 shows $26,443 state-shared, convention center column confidential
deadline_pattern: No deadline; applications are emailed to selahparks@selahwa.gov and heard at the next regular LTAC meeting (fourth Monday, 11:00 a.m.) or a special meeting. Funds are approved only for the current calendar year, so apply well ahead of the event and ideally early in the year.
annual_pool: About $26,000 a year in revenue (2024 DOR); 2024 awards included $20,000 to Selah Community Days and $7,005 of a $15,914 Yakima Valley Tourism request
contact: Selah Parks & Recreation, selahparks@selahwa.gov (Zack Schab, Recreation Manager/Director, staffed the 2024 meetings); Selah City Hall
notes: Selah runs a small rolling program through Parks & Recreation: submit the Application for LTAC Funds (fillable PDF) to selahparks@selahwa.gov, then present the project at the LTAC meeting where it is reviewed. The committee approves by motion at the meeting, funds only the listed event and date in the current year, and reimburses against receipts (advertising and flyers up to 100%, dated promo items 50%, vendor deposits 100%); post-event reports are due January 31. Awards have gone to Selah Community Days ($20,000), the Selah Downtown Association's 4th of July and Yakima Valley Tourism packages. The form lists government, 501(c)(3), 501(c)(6) and 'other' applicant types, so for-profit status is unclear.
members_source: https://selahwa.gov/tourism/lodging-tax-advisory-committee-ltac (LTAC members section; Recreation Director sits as non-voting adjunct)

presentation.pattern: Applicant presents at the LTAC meeting where the application is reviewed; email selahparks@selahwa.gov for the date and time
presentation.format: In-person presentation at Selah City Council Chambers, 11:00 a.m. regular meetings; no length published

meeting_schedule: Regular meetings fourth Monday of every month at 11:00 a.m., Selah City Council Chambers; special meetings as needed (e.g., Friday May 31, 2024 at 3:00 p.m.)
pool_note: $26,443 is the 2024 DOR distribution; no fund balance published. The city itself applies for 4th of July fireworks and pays Yakima Valley Tourism dues from the same fund, so the outside-applicant share is smaller than revenue and not computable from public records.

name: Twisp
tax_rate: 4% (2% state-shared plus 2% special hotel/motel tax per DOR rate flyer and TMC 3.30); in September 2025 the mayor described the rate as 2% and floated raising it to 4%, so the special tax may have been adopted after that; DOR 2024 shows $23,613 state-shared and $23,574 special
deadline_pattern: No application process; the town council allocates the fund directly during fall budget deliberations (September-December)
annual_pool: 2024 revenue $47,186; 2025 budgeted $42,000 against $68,539 in expenses; fund in deficit
contact: Town of Twisp, Mayor Hans Smith; Town Hall
notes: Twisp has no grant program and no LTAC (population under 5,000). The council spends the roughly $42,000-$47,000 a year directly: a contract with the Twisp Chamber of Commerce ($25,000 for 2026, down from $30,000, for Twispfest, Mistletoe Madness and the 4th of July parade), $2,000 to the Creative District, $1,000 to the Tree Board, and the largest line, about $16,000-plus for public restroom cleaning. Revenue fell 13% from 2021 to 2024 while expenses rose 35%, the fund is running a deficit, and in December 2025 the mayor told the Chamber not to count on lodging tax money in 2027. An outside event would have to be pitched to the council directly, and the money is not there; Okanogan County's LTAC is the realistic route.
meeting_schedule: No LTAC; Town Council meets the second and fourth Tuesdays at 5:30 p.m.
pool_note: 2024 revenue $47,186 (town packet; DOR agrees at $47,186). 2025 budget committed $25,000 Chamber, $2,000 Creative District, $1,000 Tree Board and about $40,000 for restrooms and facilities, exceeding revenue; nothing is set aside for outside applicants.

tax_rate: City share of state lodging tax; DOR 2024 shows $0 state-shared and $33,324 special, listed under King County
deadline_pattern: Two windows a year: applications received March 1-31 fund projects running July-December, and applications received August 1-31 fund projects running January-June of the next year; projects must be completed within the budget year (Jan 1-Dec 31)
annual_pool: Not published; program funded from the city's share of state lodging tax (2024 distributions $33,324)
contact: Beth Wright, Finance, City of Pacific, bwright@pacificwa.gov, (253) 929-1117; mail to City of Pacific, Attn: Finance Director, 100 3rd Avenue SE, Pacific, WA 98047; City Hall (253) 929-1100
notes: Pacific launched a Tourism Promotion Grant Program in 2026 for tourism projects and events within city limits, funded by the city's share of state lodging tax. It runs two application windows a year (March 1-31 for July-December projects, August 1-31 for January-June projects); the Lodging Tax Advisory Committee (also called the Tax and Tourism Board) meets ad hoc when projects are identified, recommends to council, and council may fund all, part or none of a request. Nonprofits, for-profits, individuals and groups are all eligible, awards are competitive, and applicants are notified after the council vote. No committee roster, pool size or award cap is published; the information packet PDF could not be fetched in this session.

name: Cashmere
tax_rate: 4% (2% state-shared plus 2% special hotel/motel tax per DOR rate flyer); DOR 2024 distribution figures confidential
annual_pool: City hotel/motel tax budgeted at $5,000 a year (2018 and 2019 city revenue reports); DOR 2024 figures confidential
notes: Cashmere's own hotel/motel tax is tiny: the city budgeted $5,000 a year in 2018 and 2019 and collected $3,503 through October 2018, so there is no city grant program and no LTAC activity was found. The working route for a Cashmere event is Chelan County's Event & Marketing Grant, which in 2026 sent $20,588 to Cashmere groups (Cashmere Chamber Christmas in Cashmere $5,000, Cashmere Community Concerts Wenatchee River Bluegrass Festival $8,588, Cashmere Museum & Pioneer Village marketing $2,000, Leavenworth & Cashmere Farmers Markets $5,000) out of $221,638 awarded to 43 recipients; the county framework also gives the Cashmere Chamber 3% of county lodging tax directly.

name: Colfax
tax_rate: 2% state-shared plus a 2% special hotel/motel tax on businesses with 30 or more rooms (DOR rate flyer); DOR 2024 shows $28,015 state-shared and $17,783 special
deadline_pattern: Historically an annual fall call: applications due Friday Sept 16, 2016 (5 p.m.) with committee deliberation Sept 20, and due Oct 6 in 2017, for the following year's projects. Current cycle dates not found.
typical_open: Late August to mid-September (2016 and 2017 cycles)
annual_pool: Roughly $40,000 a year per the city in 2017; 2024 DOR distributions $45,798
contact: Colfax City Administrator, Colfax City Hall, 400 N. Mill Street, Colfax, WA 99111 (2016-2017 contacts were Mike Rizzitiello and Dodd Snodgrass; current administrator not verified)
notes: Colfax runs its lodging tax through a council-created Economic Development, Tourism and Events Committee that issues an annual call for proposals in late summer, deliberates at a public meeting at City Hall and sends recommendations to council. Proposals must draw overnight paid-lodging visitors from more than 50 miles away and applicants need a federal tax ID; forms were posted on the city website and Facebook page. The program was documented in 2016 and 2017 Whitman County Gazette coverage; nothing more recent was found before this session's search budget ran out, so confirm the committee still operates and get the 2027 dates from City Hall.
meeting_schedule: Committee deliberates once a year in September or October (Sept 20, 2016 at 5:30 p.m., City Hall)
pool_note: $45,798 is the 2024 DOR distribution; the city described the fund as roughly $40,000 a year in 2017. No award list or set-asides found.
